mainTopic: רבי שמעון's source for a כהן pouring the oil, and רב's rule that תורה and חוקה make a step לעכב
overview: The גמרא first looks for רבי שמעון's source for requiring a כהן to pour the oil on a מנחה. Reading 'הכהנים' in both directions fails, because אביי shows that רבי שמעון reads a פסוק only forward. So the גמרא says his source is the ו in 'וְהֵבִיאָהּ', which links back to the pouring. It then explains why that ו does not make שחיטה need a כהן: שחיטה is linked to סמיכה. A קל וחומר from זריקה and a פסוק about יום הכפורים show that the owner does not have to slaughter either. Next comes a new topic: רב's rule that the words תורה and חוקה make a step לעכב. Using the cases of נזיר, תודה, מצורע, יום הכפורים and the other קרבנות, the גמרא arrives at this reading: חוקה alone is enough, but תורה alone is not. It then tests this rule against מנחה and לחם הפנים, and begins explaining why מנחה is different from the words 'מגרשה ומשמנה'. That explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The word 'the priests' applies both before and after
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its explanation of רבי שמעון's view. The word 'הכהנים' in the פסוק is read both backward and forward.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The priests': the verse is read as applying to what comes before it and to what comes after it.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of an explanation that started just before this point. It explains why רבי שמעון requires a כהן for pouring the oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, pouring the oil (יציקה) comes before the word 'הכהנים' and taking the handful (קמיצה) comes after it. If 'הכהנים' is read in both directions, then both jobs need a כהן. This depends on the rule מקרא נדרש לפניו ולאחריו.

keyTerms.meaning: A word in a verse is read as applying to what comes before it and to what comes after it
'The priests', the word in the פסוק being read in both directions
Pouring the oil onto the מנחה
Taking a handful from the מנחה

steps.whyThisMatters: The whole next challenge is about whether רבי שמעון really accepts this two-direction reading.

phrases.english: 'The priests':
phrases.notes: This finishes a פסוק quoted just before: 'and he shall bring it to the sons of אהרן, the priests'.

phrases.english: the verse is read as applying to what comes before it and to what comes after it.
phrases.notes: Before 'the priests' comes pouring the oil, and after it comes taking the handful. So both need a כהן.

steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי שמעון, pouring the oil needs a כהן because 'הכהנים' also applies backward to the pouring.

steps.title: Challenge: does רבי שמעון really read verses in both directions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי שמעון actually holds this rule. It brings a ברייתא where the רבנן read 'with his finger' both backward and forward.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי שמעון really hold that a verse is read both before and after? But a ברייתא teaches: 'And the כהן shall take of the blood of the חטאת with his finger and put it on the corners of the altar.' 'With his finger… and shall take' teaches that collecting the blood must be done only with the right hand. 'With his finger… and put' teaches that placing the blood must be done only with the right hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation from step 1. It is setting up a ברייתא that will show רבי שמעון does not read verses backward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, 'and shall take' comes before 'with his finger', and 'and put' comes after it. The first opinion in the ברייתא reads 'finger' in both directions, so both collecting (קבלה) and placing (נתינה) must be done with the right hand. The next step shows where רבי שמעון stands on this.

Placing the blood on the altar
The right hand
'With his finger', the word read in both directions
The corners of the altar

steps.title: רבי שמעון: collecting with the left hand is valid
steps.stepSummary: In the same ברייתא, רבי שמעון disagrees. He says collecting the blood with the left hand is valid, because the hand-word is not said about collecting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: Is 'hand' said about collecting? Since 'hand' is not said about collecting, if he collected with the left hand, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with רבי שמעון's opinion. He does not apply 'with his finger' to collecting the blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון ties the right-hand rule only to placing the blood, which comes after 'with his finger'. He does not tie it to collecting, which comes before. This is the evidence the גמרא uses against step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: The left hand
Valid
Since

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון is not saying the word 'finger' is missing from the פסוק. He is saying it does not apply to collecting, which comes before it in the verse.

phrases.english: רבי שמעון said:
Is 'hand' said about collecting?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי שמעון's disagreement with the reading in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Collecting the blood with the left hand is valid. Only placing the blood needs the right hand.

steps.title: אביי: they disagree about reading in both directions
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the disagreement in the ברייתא is about whether a verse is read in both directions. רבי שמעון reads only forward.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי said: They disagree about whether a verse is read as applying before it and after it. רבי שמעון holds it is read as applying after it, but not before it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes its challenge with אביי's statement. That statement shows רבי שמעון does not read verses backward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי שמעון reads only forward, then 'הכהנים' cannot apply backward to pouring the oil. So the explanation in step 1 of why he requires a כהן for pouring the oil seems to fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: They disagree
It is read as applying to what comes after it
It is not read as applying to what comes before it

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן read a verse in both directions. רבי שמעון reads it only forward. That makes it hard to explain his view on pouring the oil using 'הכהנים'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the need for a new explanation of רבי שמעון's requirement that a כהן pour the oil.

phrases.english: They disagree about whether a verse is read as applying to what comes before it and after it.

steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון does not hold מקרא נדרש לפניו

steps.title: A new source for רבי שמעון: the ו links back
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי שמעון does not read a פסוק in both directions, the גמרא says his source is the ו in 'וְהֵבִיאָהּ', which adds onto the earlier matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is רבי שמעון's reason: 'And he shall bring it.' The 'and' (ו) adds onto the matter before it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי שמעון a different source for why the pouring of oil must be done by a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The old explanation, reading 'הכהנים' both backward and forward, failed in Step 4. Now the 'and' at the start of 'וְהֵבִיאָהּ' ties the earlier actions, such as pouring the oil, to the כהנים mentioned next. So the pouring also needs a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: The letter vav ('and') adds onto the matter before it and links the two together

Pouring the oil onto the מנחה

phrases.english: the vav adds onto the earlier matter.

steps.terutzResolutionType: New source for the same ruling

steps.terutzMaskana: His source is the linking vav in 'וְהֵבִיאָהּ'

steps.title: If ו links back, slaughter by a זר should be invalid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges whether רבי שמעון holds the ו rule. In the פסוק about the עולה, the ו would link שחיטה to the כהנים, yet שחיטה is valid by a זר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי שמעון really hold that ו adds onto the earlier matter? If so, look at the פסוק: 'And he shall slaughter the bull, and אהרן's sons the כהנים shall bring the blood and sprinkle the blood.' We learn from it that from collecting the blood onward is the job of the כהנים, which teaches that שחיטה is valid by a זר. But if for רבי שמעון ו adds onto the earlier matter, then שחיטה by a זר should also be invalid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new source from Step 5. The same ו rule would wrongly make a זר's שחיטה invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ויקרא 1:5 the word 'וְהִקְרִיבוּ' also starts with a ו. If that ו links back, then 'הכהנים' would cover the שחיטה before it. But everyone agrees שחיטה is valid by a זר, since the כהן's work only starts at קבלה.

A non-kohen

phrases.english: then slaughter by a non-priest should also be invalid!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וָיו מוֹסִיף עַל עִנְיָן רִאשׁוֹן

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Applied to ויקרא 1:5, the rule would make שחיטה need a כהן. That contradicts the accepted law that a זר may slaughter.

steps.title: Slaughter is different: it is linked to סמיכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שחיטה is an exception. The פסוק puts 'וְסָמַךְ' right next to 'וְשָׁחַט', so just as סמיכה is done by non-כהנים, שחיטה is too.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the פסוק says: 'And he shall lean... and he shall slaughter.' Just as leaning is done by non-כהנים, so too slaughter is done by non-כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי שמעון by showing a special source that makes שחיטה valid by a זר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ו rule still holds in general. For שחיטה, though, a stronger link to סמיכה, which the owner does and not a כהן, shows that non-כהנים may slaughter. That link overrides the ו for this case.

keyTerms.meaning: Leaning one's hands on the head of the קרבן
'It is different there'. The case is an exception
Two things placed side by side in a פסוק so that they share the same law

phrases.english: It is different there, for the verse says:
"And he shall lean... and he shall slaughter,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:4–5

phrases.english: just as leaning is done by non-priests,
so too slaughter is done by non-priests.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם, דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 6

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ו rule would make שחיטה need a כהן
steps.terutzMaskana: The link to סמיכה shows that a זר may slaughter, so the ו rule still stands elsewhere

steps.title: Should only the owner slaughter, like סמיכה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: if שחיטה is compared to סמיכה, then just as only the owner does סמיכה, only the owner should be allowed to slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, just as leaning is done by the owners, slaughter should also be done only by the owners?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the comparison from Step 7, which seems to prove too much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If סמיכה and שחיטה are linked, why copy only the part where it is not done by a כהן? סמיכה is done only by the owner, so the link should limit שחיטה to the owner as well.

keyTerms.meaning: The owner who brings the קרבן

phrases.english: If so: just as leaning is done by the owners,
so too slaughter should be done only by the owners?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי: מָה סְמִיכָה בִּבְעָלִים, אַף שְׁחִיטָה בִּבְעָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the comparison used in Step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: The הֶקֵּשׁ between סמיכה and שחיטה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the two are fully compared, שחיטה should also need the owner, which is not the law

steps.title: A קל וחומר from sprinkling: no owner needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a קל וחומר. זריקה is the main act of atonement and does not need the owner, so שחיטה, which is not the main act, certainly does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You cannot say that, because of a קל וחומר. Sprinkling the blood is the main atonement, yet it does not need the owner. Slaughter is not the main atonement, so all the more so it does not need the owner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge of Step 8 and shows that the owner does not need to do the שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן does the זריקה, which is the most important act, on the owner's behalf. If the owner is not needed for the most important act, he is surely not needed for a less important one. So the comparison to סמיכה only teaches that a זר may slaughter, not that only the owner may.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a weaker case to a stronger one
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח
The main act that brings atonement
'Is it not all the more so?'

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, the ו in 'וְהֵבִיאָהּ' makes pouring the oil a job for a כהן. שחיטה is an exception, because its link to סמיכה shows a זר may slaughter. A קל וחומר from זריקה shows the owner does not have to be the one who slaughters.

phrases.english: That you cannot say,
because of a קל וחומר:
if sprinkling, which is the main act of atonement,
does not need the owners,
then slaughter, which is not the main act of atonement,
is it not all the more so?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא לָא מָצֵית אָמַרְתָּ, קַל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: קַל וָחוֹמֶר limits how far the הֶקֵּשׁ reaches
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The link to סמיכה would require the owner to slaughter
steps.terutzMaskana: The owner is not needed for שחיטה, since he is not even needed for זריקה

steps.title: Maybe we cannot learn from זריקה, which the owner cannot do anyway
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a possible problem with the קל וחומר from step 9. זריקה never needs the owner simply because the owner is usually not a כהן. שחיטה is something the owner is able to do, so maybe it still needs him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: we cannot learn something that is possible from something that is impossible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against its own קל וחומר. This step sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר said: זריקה is the main act and does not need the owner, so surely שחיטה does not. But the owner cannot do זריקה at all, because only a כהן may do it. So זריקה tells us nothing about an act the owner is able to do, like שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you will say' — the גמרא raises an objection before anyone asks it
We cannot learn a case where something is possible from a case where it is impossible
Throwing the blood on the מזבח

phrases.english: And if you would say
one cannot derive the possible from the impossible
phrases.notes: The owner usually can't do זריקה, since he isn't a כהן, but he can slaughter. So maybe זריקה proves nothing about שחיטה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא, אֵין דָּנִין אֶפְשָׁר מִשֶּׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the קל וחומר of step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The קל וחומר from זריקה to שחיטה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Learning from זריקה fails, because the owner is not allowed to do זריקה in the first place. Its lack of need for the owner is no proof for שחיטה, which the owner is able to do.

steps.title: יום הכפורים shows that שחיטה normally does not need the owner
steps.stepSummary: On יום הכפורים the תורה says specially that the כהן גדול slaughters his own bull. This shows that in general, שחיטה does not need the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תורה revealed regarding יום הכפורים: 'And he shall slaughter the bull of the חטאת which is his.' We learn from this that ordinary שחיטה does not need the owner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection with a פסוק about יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every שחיטה needed the owner, there would be no need to say that the כהן גדול slaughters his own bull. Since the תורה had to say it there, the rule must be that normally anyone may slaughter. This proves the point directly from a פסוק, without relying on the challenged קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: The תורה revealed, meaning it said so openly
By inference — we learn the general rule from the special case
The owner of the קרבן

steps.whatToRemember: שחיטה does not need the owner or a כהן. Only on יום הכפורים did the תורה specially ask the כהן גדול to slaughter his own bull.

phrases.english: The Merciful One revealed regarding Yom Kippur:
"And he shall slaughter the bull of the sin offering which is his"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:11

phrases.english: By inference, slaughter in general
does not require the owner.

steps.triggerLanguage: גַּלִּי רַחֲמָנָא בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 10.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe שחיטה, which the owner is able to do, still requires him.
steps.terutzMaskana: The special mention on יום הכפורים shows that normally שחיטה does not need the owner.

steps.title: רב: the words תורה and חוקה make a step indispensable
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches a general rule. Wherever the תורה uses the words 'תורה' and 'חוקה' about a קרבן, that step is לעכב: without it, the קרבן is not valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: Wherever 'תורה' and 'חוקה' are said, it comes only to make the step indispensable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: רב's rule for knowing which steps are לעכב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה listed steps of a מנחה that are not לעכב. רב gives a tool for telling which steps are לעכב: look for the words תורה and חוקה in the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Indispensable: if this step is missing, the קרבן is not valid
'Law' — a word in the פסוק that shows a fixed procedure
'Statute' — a word in the פסוק that shows a fixed requirement

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the measuring stick for all the questions that follow on the נזיר, תודה, מצורע and others.

phrases.english: Rav said:
Any place where "law" and "statute" are stated,
it is only to make it indispensable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר תּוֹרָה וְחוּקָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic, connected to the משנה's list of steps that are not לעכב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The words תורה and חוקה in a פסוק make that step לעכב.

steps.title: First assumption: both words are needed together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא first assumes that רב means both words must appear together, as in the פסוק about the פרה אדומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We first thought both words are needed, as it is written: 'This is the חוקה of the תורה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a first assumption about רב's rule. This sets up the challenges that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'קא סלקא דעתין' means 'we thought at first'. So this is a starting idea that may be changed later. The first idea is that only a place with both תורה and חוקה, like 'זאת חקת התורה', counts as לעכב.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It entered our mind' — a first assumption that may be changed later
Both are needed

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the final answer. It is only what the גמרא assumes at first, and the next steps test it.

phrases.english: It entered our mind
that both are required,
as it is written: "This is the statute of the law."
phrases.notes: במדבר 19:2, about the פרה אדומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתִּין תַּרְתֵּי בָּעֲיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how to read רב's rule from step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First assumption: the step is לעכב only where both תורה and חוקה are written.

steps.title: A memory sign for the coming questions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a memory sign of letters. Each letter stands for one of the cases it will use to test רב's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory sign: נ״ת״ץ י״ק״מ״ל.)
steps.whatsHappening: This is not an argument. It is a list of letters that helps the learner remember the order of the questions coming next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each letter stands for a case: נזיר, תודה, מצורע, יום הכפורים, קרבנות, מנחה, לחם הפנים. The first case, נזיר, comes right away.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory sign to remember the order of the discussion

phrases.english: (Mnemonic: Nun Tav Tzadi, Yod Kuf Mem Lamed.)
phrases.notes: The letters stand for נזיר, תודה, מצורע, יום הכפורים, קרבנות, מנחה and לחם הפנים, in the order the גמרא discusses them.

steps.triggerLanguage: סִימָן: נת״ץ יקמ״ל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Prepares the list of challenges to the assumption in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A memory sign for the order of the cases.

steps.title: The נזיר: only 'תורה' is written, yet תנופה is indispensable
steps.stepSummary: About the נזיר the פסוק says only 'תורה', not 'חוקה'. Yet רב himself rules that the נזיר's תנופה is לעכב. This goes against the assumption that both words are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at the נזיר: only 'תורה' is written about him. And yet רב said that תנופה for a נזיר is indispensable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first assumption using the first case in the memory sign, the נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both words were needed, the נזיר's תנופה should not be לעכב, since only 'תורה' appears there. But רב rules that it is לעכב. So either one word is enough, or something else is going on.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But look at' — brings a case that seems to go against the rule
A person who took a נזירות vow and brings קרבנות when it ends
Waving the קרבן parts back and forth

phrases.english: But there is the nazirite,
about whom only "law" is written,
phrases.notes: במדבר 6:21

phrases.english: and Rav said:
waving for a nazirite is indispensable!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי נָזִיר, דְּלָא כְּתִיבָא בֵּיהּ אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the assumption from step 13 with the first case of the memory sign.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that both תורה and חוקה are needed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב makes the נזיר's תנופה לעכב even though only 'תורה' is written there.

steps.title: 'כן יעשה' counts like the word חוקה
steps.stepSummary: The נזיר is different. The פסוק also says 'כן יעשה' ('so he must do'), and that counts as if 'חוקה' were written.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there. Since it is written 'כן יעשה', it is as if 'חוקה' were written about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the נזיר does really have two words: 'תורה' plus 'כן יעשה', which acts like 'חוקה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'כן יעשה' means 'this is exactly how it must be done'. That carries the same meaning as חוקה. So the נזיר fits the rule that both words are needed, and the assumption stands for now.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is different there' — explaining why a case does not break the rule
'So he must do' — words that require doing it exactly this way
It is as if it were written

steps.whatToRemember: For the נזיר, 'תורה' together with 'כן יעשה' works like 'תורה' and 'חוקה', so his תנופה is לעכב.

phrases.english: It is different there,
since it is written "so he must do,"
phrases.notes: These words come at the end of the same פסוק, במדבר 6:21.

phrases.english: it is as if "statute" were written about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם, כֵּיוָן דִּכְתִיב כֵּן יַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about the נזיר in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Equivalent wording: another phrase does the job of חוקה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The נזיר has only 'תורה', so his case seems to break the rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'כן יעשה' counts like חוקה, so the נזיר fits the rule that both words are needed.

steps.title: Challenge from the thanks offering
steps.stepSummary: The תודה has only the word 'תורה', yet its four kinds of loaves are לעכב.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the תודה? Only 'תורה' is written about it, and yet we learned in a משנה that the four kinds of loaves of the תודה each hold the others back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another case against the idea that both words are needed. The תודה has only 'תורה', but its loaves are still לעכב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רב needs both 'תורה' and 'חוקה', the תודה's loaves should not be לעכב. The משנה says they are. So the assumption from step 13 is under attack again.

keyTerms.meaning: The thanks offering, which is brought with four kinds of loaves
They hold each other back: if one is missing, the whole מצוה is not done
'But what about...': opens a challenge from a case

phrases.english: But what about the thanks offering,
where only 'law' is written about it,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:11, 'זאת תורת זבח השלמים'.

phrases.english: and we learned in a Mishnah:
the four kinds of loaves of the thanks offering
each hold the others back.
phrases.notes: If even one kind is missing, none of them work.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי תּוֹדָה, דְּלָא כְּתִיבָא בֵּיהּ אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the נזיר was answered, the גמרא brings the next case from the memory sign.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of רב that both 'תורה' and 'חוקה' are needed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תודה has only 'תורה', yet its loaves are לעכב, so one word seems to be enough.

steps.title: The thanks offering is linked to the nazirite
steps.stepSummary: The תודה is compared to the נזיר's offering, so it shares the נזיר's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תודה is different, because it is compared to the נזיר. The פסוק says 'with the sacrifice of his thanks peace offerings', and the Master said: 'his peace offerings' comes to include the peace offering of the נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the תודה gets its rule through a link to the נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word 'שלמיו' ties the תודה to the שלמי נזיר. The נזיר already counts as having 'חוקה' because of 'כן יעשה' (step 16). So the תודה shares that strong rule, and the assumption that both words are needed survives.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different: this case has a special reason
It is compared through a הֶקֵּשׁ, a link between two things in the פסוק
To include: the word comes to add something
The peace offering the נזיר brings at the end of his נזירות

phrases.english: The thanks offering is different,
since it is compared to the nazirite,
as it is written:
"With the sacrifice of his peace offerings for thanksgiving,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:13.

phrases.english: and the Master said:
"His peace offerings" comes to include the peace offering of the nazirite.
phrases.notes: The נזיר already counts as having 'חוקה' because of 'כן יעשה' (step 16), so the תודה is pulled along with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי תּוֹדָה דְּאִיתַּקַּשׁ לְנָזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the תודה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תודה has only 'תורה', so it should not be לעכב under the both-words reading.
steps.terutzMaskana: Through the link to the נזיר, the תודה shares the נזיר's 'חוקה'-level rule.

steps.title: Challenge from the leper
steps.stepSummary: The מצורע has only 'תורה', yet his four kinds are לעכב.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the מצורע? Only 'תורה' is written about him, and yet we learned in a משנה that the four kinds used for the מצורע each hold the others back!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the next case against the both-words reading. The מצורע has only 'תורה', but his four kinds are לעכב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of challenge as the תודה, but now there is no link to the נזיר to rescue it. If only 'תורה' is written, the both-words reading says it should not be לעכב.

keyTerms.meaning: A person with צרעת who goes through a purification process
Four kinds: the four items used in the מצורע's purification

phrases.english: But what about the leper,
where only 'law' is written about him,
and we learned in a Mishnah:
the four kinds used for the leper
phrases.notes: Cedar wood, hyssop, red wool and the birds.

phrases.english: each hold the others back!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי מְצוֹרָע, דְּלָא כְּתִיב בֵּיהּ אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next case from the memory sign, after the תודה was answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of רב that both words are needed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מצורע has only 'תורה', yet his four kinds are לעכב.

steps.title: The extra word 'shall be' counts as 'statute'
steps.stepSummary: 'זאת תהיה תורת המצורע' has the extra word 'תהיה', which counts like 'חוקה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: There it is different, since it is written 'זאת תהיה תורת המצרע', 'This shall be the law of the leper'. It is as if 'חוקה' were written about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the מצורע's פסוק has extra strong wording that counts like 'חוקה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'תהיה' ('shall be') makes the command firm, just like 'כן יעשה' did for the נזיר. So the מצורע really has both 'תורה' and something equal to 'חוקה'. The both-words reading still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Shall be': an extra word that makes the command firm
It is as if it were written: treated the same as if the word appeared
There: in that case

phrases.english: There it is different,
since it is written:
"This shall be the law of the leper,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:2. The key word is 'תהיה', 'shall be'.

phrases.english: it is as if 'statute' were written about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם, כֵּיוָן דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the מצורע, using the same idea as the נזיר answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra word in the פסוק counts as 'חוקה'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מצורע has only 'תורה', so it should not be לעכב.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'תהיה' counts like 'חוקה', so the מצורע has both.

steps.title: Challenge from the two goats of Yom Kippur
steps.stepSummary: יום הכפורים has only 'חוקה', yet the two שעירים are לעכב.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about יום הכפורים? Only 'חוקה' is written about it, and yet we learned in a משנה that the two goats of יום הכפורים each hold the other back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a case from the other side: here only 'חוקה' is written, with no 'תורה' at all, and still it is לעכב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now each case had 'תורה' and the גמרא found something like 'חוקה'. Here there is no 'תורה' and no way to find one. This case breaks the idea that both words are needed, and the גמרא does not answer it; it changes its reading in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The two goats of יום הכפורים: one for ה' and one sent to עזאזל
Statute: one of the two key words in רב's rule

phrases.english: But what about Yom Kippur,
where only 'statute' is written about it,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:29, 'והיתה לכם לחקת עולם'.

phrases.english: and we learned in a Mishnah:
the two goats of Yom Kippur
each hold the other back.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, דְּלָא כְּתִיב בֵּיהּ אֶלָּא חוּקָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next case from the memory sign; this one cannot be answered under the both-words reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of רב that both words are needed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only 'חוקה' is written, yet the goats are לעכב, so one word must be enough.

steps.title: New reading: either word is enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops its first reading: רב means either 'תורה' or 'חוקה' makes it לעכב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב means: either 'תורה' or 'חוקה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up the idea that both words are needed and offers a new reading of רב: one word alone is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case of יום הכפורים could not be explained, so the assumption from step 13 is dropped. The new reading easily covers every case so far. But it will be tested right away in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: the גמרא drops the old idea and offers a new one
Either... or: one of the two is enough

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the final answer. The גמרא is about to challenge this new reading too, and it will end up in between: 'חוקה' alone is enough, but 'תורה' alone is not.

phrases.english: Rather:
either 'law' or 'statute'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: אוֹ תּוֹרָה אוֹ חוּקָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the יום הכפורים challenge by changing the reading of רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Either word on its own is enough.

steps.title: Challenge from the other offerings
steps.stepSummary: Other קרבנות have 'תורה' written about them, yet their steps are not לעכב.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the other קרבנות? 'תורה' is written about them, and yet their steps do not hold each other back!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new either-word reading using the regular קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'זאת התורה לעלה למנחה...' about many קרבנות. If 'תורה' alone were enough, all their steps would be לעכב, but they are not. So 'תורה' alone cannot be enough.

keyTerms.meaning: The rest of the קרבנות: עולה, מנחה, חטאת, אשם and so on
They do not hold back: missing a step does not make the קרבן invalid

phrases.english: But what about the rest of the offerings,
where 'law' is written about them,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:37, 'זאת התורה לעלה למנחה ולחטאת ולאשם'.

phrases.english: and yet they do not hold each other back?

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי שְׁאָר קׇרְבָּנוֹת, דִּכְתִיב בְּהוּ תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the new reading given in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that either word alone is enough
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Regular קרבנות have 'תורה' but are not לעכב, so 'תורה' alone cannot be enough.

steps.title: 'Law' needs 'statute', but 'statute' stands alone
steps.stepSummary: 'תורה' alone is not enough and needs 'חוקה'; 'חוקה' alone is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'תורה' needs 'חוקה' too, but 'חוקה' does not need 'תורה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a new reading of רב: 'חוקה' by itself makes a step לעכב, but 'תורה' only works together with 'חוקה'. The next steps go on to test this reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits every case. The regular קרבנות have only 'תורה', so they are not לעכב. יום הכפורים has 'חוקה', so it is לעכב. The נזיר, תודה and מצורע have 'תורה' plus something that counts as 'חוקה', so they are לעכב.

keyTerms.meaning: Needs: requires something more
Law: one of the two key words; on its own it is not enough

steps.whatToRemember: New reading of רב: 'חוקה' alone makes a step לעכב. 'תורה' alone does not; it works only together with 'חוקה' or a word that counts like 'חוקה', such as 'כן יעשה' or 'תהיה'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains all the earlier answers: the גמרא worked so hard to find 'חוקה' for the נזיר and the מצורע because 'תורה' by itself would not have been enough.

phrases.english: 'Law' needs 'statute',
but 'statute' does not need 'law'.

steps.triggerLanguage: תּוֹרָה בָּעֲיָא חוּקָּה, וְחוּקָּה לָא בָּעֲיָא תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the other קרבנות and settles the meaning of רב's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Refining the rule: the two words are not equal
steps.terutzMaskana: 'חוקה' alone is enough; 'תורה' needs 'חוקה' with it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Only 'חוקה', or 'תורה' together with 'חוקה', makes a step לעכב.

steps.title: But רב said both words, 'תורה' and 'חוקה'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that 'חוקה' alone is enough, because רב mentioned both 'תורה' and 'חוקה' together.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב said 'תורה and חוקה' (both together)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. רב's own words name both 'תורה' and 'חוקה', so it sounds like he needs both, not 'חוקה' alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 24 the גמרא said 'חוקה' alone is enough to make the steps לעכב. But רב's rule was worded as 'wherever it says תורה and חוקה'. If 'חוקה' alone were enough, why would רב mention 'תורה' at all?

keyTerms.meaning: But look! (opens a challenge from something already known)
'Law and statute': the two words in רב's rule

phrases.english: But he said 'law and statute'!
phrases.notes: 'He' is רב.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא תּוֹרָה וְחוּקָּה קָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 24's claim that 'חוקה' alone is enough.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 24: 'חוקה' alone makes the steps לעכב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב's wording joins 'תורה' and 'חוקה', which suggests both words are needed.

steps.title: Even where 'תורה' is written, 'חוקה' is what decides
steps.stepSummary: רב means: even if 'תורה' appears, the steps are לעכב only when 'חוקה' is also written.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רב means: even though 'תורה' is written, if 'חוקה' is written, yes (it is לעכב); and if not, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רב's wording. He mentions 'תורה' only to say that 'תורה' by itself does not help; 'חוקה' is what counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב is not saying both words are required. He is saying that 'תורה' alone is not enough, and only 'חוקה' makes the steps לעכב. This keeps step 24's position and fits רב's words.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means (the גמרא reads someone's words in a new way)
Even though
Yes / no

steps.whatToRemember: Final shape of רב's rule so far: 'חוקה' is what makes the steps לעכב. 'תורה' alone does not.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
Even though 'law' is written,
if 'statute' is written, yes (it is לעכב);
phrases.notes: 'Yes' means not doing the steps ruins the קרבן.

phrases.english: and if not, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: אַף עַל גַּב דִּכְתִיב תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 25 by reading רב's words differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of רב's statement
steps.terutzMaskana: רב means that even where 'תורה' appears, only 'חוקה' makes the steps לעכב.

steps.title: מנחה has 'חוקה', yet רב needed repetition to make it לעכב
steps.stepSummary: 'חוקה' is written by מנחה, yet רב said its steps are לעכב only where the פסוק repeats them, which suggests 'חוקה' alone is not enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at מנחה: 'חוקה' is written about it. And רב said: every place where the פסוק repeated something in the law of מנחה, it comes only to make it לעכב. So if it repeated, yes; if it did not repeat, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge from מנחה. If 'חוקה' alone made everything לעכב, every step of a מנחה should be לעכב, but רב himself made it depend on repetition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By מנחה the word 'חוקה' appears. Yet רב taught that a step of the מנחה is לעכב only if the פסוק repeats it. That means steps that are not repeated are not לעכב, even though 'חוקה' is there. This seems to go against the rule that 'חוקה' alone is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: But look at (brings a case that seems to go against the rule)
A flour offering
The פסוק repeated (said the law a second time)

phrases.english: But look at the flour offering, where 'statute' is written about it,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:11

phrases.english: and רב said: every place
where the verse repeated something in the law of the flour offering,
phrases.notes: The laws of the מנחה are written twice in ויקרא, in chapter 2 and again in chapter 6.

phrases.english: it comes only to make it essential (לעכב).
So if it repeated, yes; if it did not repeat, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי מִנְחָה, דִּכְתִיב בָּהּ חוּקָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the wording was settled, the גמרא tests the rule against a real case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that 'חוקה' alone makes a קרבן's steps לעכב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מנחה has 'חוקה', yet רב says only repeated steps are לעכב, so 'חוקה' alone did not make all its steps לעכב.

steps.title: By מנחה, the 'חוקה' is about eating
steps.stepSummary: The 'חוקה' by מנחה refers to eating it, not to its service, so it does not make the service steps לעכב.
steps.simpleTranslation: There it is different, because when 'חוקה' is written, it is written about the eating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the מנחה question. The word 'חוקה' there is attached to eating the מנחה, so it says nothing about the service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'חוקה' makes something לעכב only for the subject it is written about. By מנחה it is written about the כהנים eating it. That is why the service steps needed a different source, the repetition of the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: There it is different
About the eating

steps.confusionAlert: This does not say 'חוקה' has no power by מנחה. It only says its power goes to the eating, not to the service.

phrases.english: There it is different,
because when 'statute' is written, it is written about the eating.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם, דְּכִי כְּתִיבָא חוּקָּה אַאֲכִילָה כְּתִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מנחה challenge of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting what the word 'חוקה' refers to
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'חוקה' by מנחה should make all its service steps לעכב.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'חוקה' by מנחה is about the eating, so the service steps need repetition to be לעכב.

steps.title: לחם הפנים has 'חוקה' about eating, yet its parts are לעכב
steps.stepSummary: By לחם הפנים, 'חוקה' is also written about eating, yet a משנה says its arrangements and bowls of לבונה are לעכב each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at לחם הפנים: there too 'חוקה' is written about the eating. And we learned in a משנה: the two arrangements hold each other back; the two bowls hold each other back; the arrangements and the bowls hold each other back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last answer. לחם הפנים is just like מנחה, with 'חוקה' written about eating, yet its parts are still לעכב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 28 said a 'חוקה' about eating does not make the service לעכב. But by לחם הפנים the 'חוקה' is also about eating, and the משנה still says the two rows of bread and the two bowls of לבונה are each needed for the other to count. So a 'חוקה' about eating seems to make the service לעכב after all.

keyTerms.meaning: The showbread placed on the שולחן in the משכן and בית המקדש
Arrangements (the two rows of six loaves)
Bowls of לבונה (frankincense) placed with the bread
They hold each other back: without one, the other does not count

phrases.english: But look at the showbread,
where when 'statute' is written, it is written about the eating,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 24:9

phrases.english: and we learned in a משנה: the two arrangements
phrases.notes: This משנה comes later in this מסכת (27a).

phrases.english: hold each other back;

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי בָּזִיכִין מְעַכְּבִין זֶה אֶת זֶה,
phrases.english: the two bowls hold each other back;

phrases.aramaic: הַסְּדָרִין וְהַבָּזִיכִין מְעַכְּבִין זֶה אֶת זֶה.
phrases.english: the arrangements and the bowls hold each other back.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים, דְּכִי כְּתִיבָא חוּקָּה אַאֲכִילָה כְּתִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 28's answer with a parallel case.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 28: a 'חוקה' written about eating does not make the service לעכב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By לחם הפנים, 'חוקה' is also about eating, yet the משנה makes its arrangements and bowls לעכב each other.

steps.title: So חוקה written about eating covers the whole קרבן
steps.stepSummary: From לחם הפנים the גמרא concludes that חוקה written about eating applies to all of the קרבן's laws, which undoes the answer given for מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, wherever חוקה is written about eating, it is written about the whole matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its challenge from לחם הפנים. It concludes that a חוקה written about eating actually applies to the entire קרבן, service included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 28 the גמרא said the חוקה by מנחה is only about eating, so it does not make the service steps לעכב. But by לחם הפנים the חוקה is also about eating, and still its steps are לעכב. So 'it's only about eating' cannot be a real limit, and the old question returns: why are the steps of מנחה not all לעכב?

keyTerms.meaning: Eating (of the קרבן)
The whole matter, meaning all the laws of the קרבן
A 'statute'; when written by a קרבן, it shows its steps are לעכב
Holding back; the step is required, and without it the קרבן is not valid

phrases.english: Rather, anywhere that
it (חוקה) is written about eating –
it is written about the whole matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, כֹּל הֵיכָא דִּכְתִיבָא אַאֲכִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion of the challenge from לחם הפנים in Step 29
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in Step 28 that the חוקה by מנחה refers only to eating
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: לחם הפנים shows that a חוקה about eating still makes the service steps לעכב, so the same should be true for מנחה. That brings back the question from Step 27.

steps.title: מנחה is different because of 'מגרשה ומשמנה'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that מנחה is a special case, because its פסוק says 'of its groats and of its oil'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the פסוק says: 'Of its groats and of its oil.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It agrees that חוקה about eating normally covers everything, but says מנחה is an exception because of a special phrase in its פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule from Step 30 stays in place: a חוקה about eating covers the whole קרבן. מנחה is not taken out of the חוקה category. It just has an unusual outcome, because the פסוק says 'its groats' and 'its oil'. The גמרא explains in the next line how these words narrow which steps are לעכב.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there; this case is an exception
The פסוק
Its groats (coarse flour) of the מנחה
Its oil

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the חוקה by מנחה has no effect. מנחה is an exception because of its own פסוק, and the general rule from Step 30 still stands.

phrases.english: It is different there,
phrases.notes: 'There' is the מנחה.

phrases.english: since the verse says:
"Of its groats and of its oil,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:16. The sentence continues in the next line of the גמרא.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם, דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 30 by treating מנחה as an exception
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case through a special wording in its פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since חוקה about eating covers everything, all the steps of מנחה should be לעכב
steps.terutzMaskana: מנחה is different because its פסוק says 'מגרשה ומשמנה', which affects which steps are לעכב (explained further on)
